subject: Nimbus incident: forensics summary, assurance checklist, and verification steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Morris <evelyn@nimbusapp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial forensics package & short RCA: Nimbus memory leak (Oct 3)

Evelyn —

Thanks again for your patience while our team completed the first-pass forensic analysis. Attaching a compact bundle of logs and an initial timeline for your engineering and legal review. Below is a short, high-level summary we wanted to share ahead of the fuller report.

Summary (TL;DR)
- What happened: An intermittent memory fragmentation issue in our sequence cache allocator caused per-worker RSS to grow on requests with large KV-cache churn, resulting in degraded inference latency and, in a few pods, OOM restarts on Oct 3 between 03:12–04:05 UTC.
- Impact: Approx. 12% of your inference requests during the window experienced increased tail latency; 3 host restarts led to transient 5–8 minute request failures for routing to those hosts.
- Root cause (short): An allocator regression in a C++ memory path introduced during a performance patch; under a specific request mix the allocator failed to release slab fragments back to the OS quickly enough.

What we're sending now
- compact log bundle with correlated node metrics and request IDs (attachment: nimbus_forensics_log_bundle.tar.gz)
- an event timeline CSV that maps request ids to host restarts (timeline_correlated_events.csv)
- an internal action checklist (rfc_action_checklist.xlsx) that lists short/medium/long term mitigations and owners

Immediate mitigations completed (what we did already)
- Rolled the affected runtime image to previous, stable allocator (completed Oct 3 04:30 UTC).
- Applied a hotfix to routing policy to avoid heavy KV-cache churn on older model versions (completed Oct 3 05:10 UTC).
- Increased observability for allocator metrics and introduced an automated alert at 70% fragmentation (completed Oct 4).

Next steps we recommend and will own
- Short (within 7 days): Release allocator safety patch to your dedicated pool, additional monitoring hooks, and a customer verification window.
- Medium (30 days): Release a quantization/allocator redesign that reduces slab churn for large request sequences.
- Long (90+ days): Add an optional memory-guard mode that hard-limits per-request KV cache growth for very high-churn request patterns.

Please let us know if you'd prefer a synchronous walkthrough of the bundle — we can schedule an engineering call (30–60m) tomorrow.

Attachments referenced: nimbus_forensics_log_bundle.tar.gz (log bundle, ~23MB), timeline_correlated_events.csv, rfc_action_checklist.xlsx

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

[Attachment: nimbus_forensics_log_bundle.tar.gz (log bundle)]

Subject: Re: Initial forensics package & short RCA: Nimbus memory leak (Oct 3)

Aditya —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the attachments. A few immediate questions from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether any customer data was present in the logs in the bundle and, if so, whether it was redacted? Our legal team will need that noted for the incident record.
2) We'd like a concise timeline that ties the exact user-visible error rates to the host restart windows (for our ops postmortem). The CSV helps, but a bullet timeline would be easier to present to executives.
3) For SLA credit consideration: what is Redwood's position and proposed calculation?

Can we get those points by EOD your time? If helpful, our engineering manager (cc'd) can hop on a 30m call.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Morris
Head of Platform Reliability, NimbusApp
evelyn@nimbusapp.com

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Nimbus Engineering <eng-team@nimbusapp.com>, Nimbus Legal <legal@nimbusapp.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Forensics summary, consolidated timeline, SLA position, and verification plan — Nimbus incident

Evelyn —

Following up with the consolidated items you requested. Below is a succinct RCA, a correlated timeline (bullet format for exec review), our SLA credit position, and a short verification plan + action owners. The attached checklist includes owner-level details and planned delivery dates.

Full RCA (concise)
- Trigger: A performance-focused allocator change introduced in v2.14.7 (deployed Sep 28) altered slab reuse heuristics. Under a workload with frequent KV cache inserts/removals and long sequences (>= 8k tokens), the allocator delayed releasing internal fragments to the OS. Over several minutes and across multiple workers, this produced steady RSS growth and eventually OOM restarts on 3 hosts.
- Why it wasn't caught: Our internal staging tests did not replicate the exact request-size mix and KV churn pattern your traffic exercised; the performance patch did not change unit tests for high-fragmentation scenarios.
- Contributing factors: high variance in sequence lengths across your routed traffic + a subtle race in the slab-release path under contention.

Correlated timeline (UTC)
- 2026-10-03T03:12:18Z — Elevated tail latency observed for region-us-east-1 (first signal).
- 2026-10-03T03:20:00Z — Autoscaling reacted as graphs showed rising RSS; routing redistributed some traffic.
- 2026-10-03T03:28:43Z — Host i-0a12f experienced OOM; kubelet restarted the inference pod (first restart).
- 2026-10-03T03:41:10Z — Second host restart (i-0b33c).
- 2026-10-03T03:58:02Z — Third host restart (i-0c77d); by now overall success rate dipped ~2.7% for affected pool.
- 2026-10-03T04:30:00Z — We rolled back allocator to stable runtime image for the pool (mitigation completed).
- 2026-10-04T02:00:00Z — Post-rollback verification and increased monitoring remained stable during a 24-hour window.

SLA position & proposed credit
- We acknowledge the service impact and propose a one-time credit equivalent to 10% of the monthly committed spend for the affected dedicated pool for the billing period containing Oct 3. Calculation basis: observed success-rate delta and duration of degraded performance; we are open to reconciling the exact figure with Nimbus finance.

Verification plan & next actions (owner / ETA)
- Action: Patch allocator to explicitly release slab fragments under high-churn (Aditya / Eng) — ETA: 2026-10-08
- Action: Release memory-guard toggle in your dedicated pool and run a 72-hour verification window with your test workload (Monica / Customer Ops) — ETA: start 2026-10-09, complete 2026-10-12
- Action: Deliver a signed evidence package (logs + metrics + APM traces) for your auditors (Marissa / Compliance) — ETA: 2026-10-09
- Action: Update our staging test suite to include KV-churn profiles that match your traffic (Engineering / Release) — ETA: 2026-10-28

What we need from Nimbus to close verification
- A 2-hour window of test traffic that exercises your heavier sequence lengths (Monica to coordinate).
- Confirmation of the account contact for receiving the final signed evidence package (legal@ or compliance@).

Attachments: rfc_action_checklist.xlsx, timeline_correlated_events.csv, nimbus_forensics_log_bundle.tar.gz

If that looks good, we'll prepare the DocuSign statement for the credit and schedule the verification window; Marissa will own the evidence package delivery.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

[Attachment: rfc_action_checklist.xlsx]
[Attachment: timeline_correlated_events.csv]

Aditya / team —

Thanks for the clear summary and for the attachments. We agree with the RCA and appreciate the proposed credit. A couple of quick confirmations:
- We'll provide a 2-hour verification slot on Oct 10 14:00–16:00 UTC and Monica can coordinate the test script.
- For legal/evidence, please route the final package to legal@nimbusapp.com and copy our compliance lead.
- We accept the proposed 10% credit as a starting point; our finance team will send a reconciliation request if any adjustments are needed.

We'll mark the incident as reviewed on our side after the verification window completes.

—Nimbus Eng (on behalf of Evelyn)
